title: Overfitting in Deep Networks — Perfect Practice, Poor Test
key_insight: A deep network overfits when training performance keeps improving while validation performance stops improving or gets worse.
body:
## Perfect Practice, Poor Test

A student repeats the practice sheet perfectly but fails when the numbers change. The answers were memorized rather than understood.

A deep network overfits when training performance keeps improving while validation performance stops improving or gets worse.

Keep a validation set separate and watch both curves. More training is helpful only while new-data behavior also improves.
common_mistakes: Overfitting means both training and validation are always perfect.
Dropout permanently deletes the same units at deployment.
The test set should guide every training decision.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Perfect Practice, Poor Test” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Deep networks have enough capacity to memorize easily, so validation and regularization are essential.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Perfect Practice, Poor Test” situation, explain Overfitting in Deep Networks without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
